title: DSA: Graphs & Traversals
description: A Graph is a non-linear data structure consisting of nodes (vertices) and edges. Graphs are used to represent networks, such as social networks or transportation paths. Key traversal algorithms include Breadth-First Search (BFS) for shortest paths and Depth-First Search (DFS) for exploring branches.
example:
# Adjacency List Representation
graph = {
  'A' : ['B','C'],
  'B' : ['D', 'E'],
  'C' : ['F'],
  'D' : [],
  'E' : ['F'],
  'F' : []
}

# BFS uses a Queue, DFS uses a Stack/Recursion.

challenges.title: BFS vs DFS
challenges.exercise: Print 'BFS uses Queue' to confirm you know the data structure used for Breadth-First Search.
